title: Fragment lifespan forecasting and prefill smoothing for paged-attention
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: reduce tail decode latency and KV churn on multi-tenant paged-attention by predicting fragment retention lifespans and applying a soft, non-blocking prefill smoothing layer. Background: current paged-KV allocator uses LRU-ish heuristics and eviction thresholds that cause oscillation when mixed short/long context workloads interleave. That oscillation increases decode stall frequency and forces conservative kernel selection, raising P95 token latency and cost. Approach: 1) Fragment Lifespan Predictor: build a lightweight online model that emits a time-to-eviction score for each fragment based on tenant, route, sequence-length histogram, and recent reuse frequency. Model is a small logistic regressor with exponentially-weighted features to keep CPU overhead minimal. 2) Micro-Residency Buckets: convert continuous lifespan scores into 4 soft buckets (hot, warm, transient, quarantine) used by the allocator to bias placement on slab ages and to choose eviction candidates. 3) Prefill Smoothing Layer: when a prefill is scheduled, apply a smoothing window that staggers prefill writes and KV-copy operations across micro-steps to avoid synchronized write spikes that cause decode interference. Prefill smoothing also consults lifespans to avoid prefetching fragments predicted to be transient. 4) Non-blocking Soft-Quarantine: introduce short, time-boxed quarantine for mid-size fragments suspected of thrashing; quarantine prevents immediate eviction while allowing background async compaction to consolidate fragments. 5) Kernel and Decode Coordination: runtime adds a lightweight hint channel where the allocator can influence kernel selection (e.g., prefer split-decode vs fused-decode) when many transient fragments are present to minimize register pressure. Telemetry and validation: add retention histograms, eviction churn counters, decode-stall traces, and predicted-vs-actual lifespan error metrics. Success criteria: reduce decode stall rate by >=30% and lower P95 token latency by >=10% on mixed workloads while keeping memory overhead <5% and CPU overhead <2% of a core. Rollout: staged canary on dedicated clusters with traffic mirroring, A/B evaluation via console rollout feature, and automatic rollback on customer-impact regression. Implementation artifacts: design doc, simulation harness, allocator patch, predictor weights saved in runtime config, dashboard. Risks: predictor misclassification causing over-retention (memory pressure) or under-retention (no improvement); increased complexity in allocator making debugging harder. Mitigations: conservative initial thresholds, safe-mode that disables smoothing on high memory pressure, unit and fuzz tests on compaction and async quarantine paths.

2025-02-25: Design review with PM (Sofia Romero) and Storage Eng (Liam O'Connor). Action: add retention histogram and per-tenant quota guard. Liam to provide slab fragmentation metrics by 2025-03-01.

2025-02-28: Prototype predictor landed in runtime branch 'prefill-lifespan-predictor'. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/876. Benchmark: +0.8% CPU, +3% memory on small frame; decode P95 improvement projected 12% on synthetic mix.

2025-03-02: Updated weights policy and added emergency safe-mode toggle. Preparing canary plan for 2025-03-06 with two dedicated clusters (canary-1 low load, canary-2 mixed load).
